stories.title: Trump suspends Russia sanctions amid dispute with Zelensky
stories.summary: Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night that suspended several sanctions against Russia that were scheduled to take effect two days later. The move prompted criticism from U.S. lawmakers and a sharp rebuke from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the United States was disregarding the sanctions. The suspension comes after a controversial U.S. deal to import Russian diesel and Ukraine’s claim that the administration is pulling back military support.
stories.why: The suspension changes the pressure tools the U.S. is using on Russia and may affect Ukraine’s expectations of continued U.S. support.
stories.previousTitle: Trump suspends pending Russia sanctions amid dispute with Ukraine
stories.previousSummary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night that suspended a number of Russia sanctions scheduled to take effect in two days. The sanctions had been passed by Congress and signed into law in September. The move drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the United States was disregarding the measures, and prompted backlash from US lawmakers. The suspension follows a recent controversial U.S. agreement to import Russian diesel and Ukrainian accusations that key military support has been withdrawn.

stories.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.summary: India will implement customs‑duty concessions for certain New Zealand imports from October 20, including zero basic duty on sheep meat, reduced rates on wine and fish, and preferential duties on manuka honey and kiwi fruit, with limited quantities permitted under tariff‑rate quotas. Dairy and other sensitive categories are excluded from the liberalisation.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.previousSummary: From 20 October, India will apply customs‑duty concessions on selected New Zealand imports under the bilateral agreement. Sheep meat will be charged zero basic customs duty, while fish, wine and manuka honey will receive specific duty rates, and kiwi fruit will be taxed at 15 percent. Dairy products are excluded from the concessions.

stories.title: Brent crude tops $110 per barrel amid Middle East tensions
stories.summary: Brent crude surpassed $110 a barrel as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed Russia‑Ukraine hostilities raised global supply concerns. WTI also rose, posting weekly gains above 10%. Goldman Sachs warned that further shipping disruptions could lift prices toward $120, while easing tensions might pull crude back toward $80.
stories.why: Higher oil prices tighten global energy markets, affecting inflation and financial markets.

stories.title: Trump grants temporary waiver of 100% tariff on Russian oil for India
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a waiver of the previously threatened 100 percent tariff on Russian oil for buyers, including India. The Global Trade and Investment (GTRI) think tank cautioned that the relief is temporary, noting that Washington could reinstate the duties at any time. GTRI pointed to U.S. purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China and ongoing India‑U.S. trade talks as possible motivations, and advised New Delhi to protect its energy security and avoid permanent trade concessions.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: RBI's forex reserves fall $60 bn in six weeks
stories.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves dropped to $726 billion on Oct 9, down from $785.7 billion on Sept 4, a decline of roughly $60 billion over six weeks. The latest reporting week alone showed a depletion of $8.58 billion.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
